cases.letter:
To: the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11; the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 38, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 7
Subject: Request for safety review at 3rd Avenue and 55th Street

Dear colleagues at NYSDOT Region 11 and NYC DOT,

Please arrange a safety study of the junction of 3rd Avenue & 55th Street, covering the approaches each agency controls: NYSDOT Region 11 for Gowanus Expressway (I 278) and BKLYN/QUEENS EXP (I 278), and NYC DOT for 3rd Avenue and 55th Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 2 November 2021 shows 90 crashes, of which 41 were injury crashes. In that period, 8 pedestrians and 1 cyclist were injured. Two people were killed in total in the official record. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is valued at $2.8 million per year. No safety work is recorded in this period. The latest recorded safety project was a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2019.

We ask you to consider two low-cost fixes on the roads you control:

* Reflective backplates on the traffic signals. This is expected to prevent about 1.2 injury crashes per year and avoid about $421,000 in harm per year, with costs recovered if each site costs under $3.0 million. Evidence is FHWA-cited.

* Longer yellow signal times. This is expected to prevent about 0.6 injury crashes per year and avoid about $219,000 in harm per year, with costs recovered if each site costs under $1.5 million. Before use, please check on site whether the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Please let us know the outcome of the site checks and any planned work.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
